scope: Screened the 538 estimator IDs and 21 documented recipes in catalogue 1.2.0 for fixed-parameter specializations, objective-family nesting and documented replacements. Listed relationships are reviewed examples, not a proof that no other mathematical inclusion exists.
policy: Display grouping only. Hide linked methods by default; restore through Show excluded and unreviewed recipes. Do not transfer validation, installation, weighting or output guarantees to the representative. A representative may have no matching executable recipe.

sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression.reason: Unpenalized least squares is the zero-penalty member of the elastic-net objective.
sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression.caveats: Family grouping only: sklearn recommends LinearRegression for alpha=0. Rank-deficient solutions, diagnostics, sparse/multioutput support and solver behavior need not match.

configuration.alpha: Ridge.alpha / n_samples for unweighted least squares

sklearn.linear_model.Ridge.reason: Ridge is the pure L2 member of the elastic-net objective.
sklearn.linear_model.Ridge.caveats: Family grouping only: use a dedicated Ridge solver in practice. Loss normalization, sample weights, solver convergence and multioutput penalties require separate mapping.

retained_distinctions: CV versus non-CV estimators retain different hyperparameter-selection behavior; do not mark a fixed estimator superseded merely by a CV wrapper.
LinearSVC/LinearSVR versus linear-kernel SVC/SVR have distinct loss, intercept, multiclass and optimization semantics.
RidgeClassifier, BayesianRidge and ARDRegression are not ordinary ElasticNet regression; preserve classification and posterior/inference semantics.
Random forests, extra trees, single trees, bagging and boosting retain distinct training, sampling and aggregation behavior.
Histogram boosting versus classical gradient boosting retain different input, approximation and training behavior.
Bayesian mixtures versus ordinary mixtures, and variational versus classical HMMs retain distinct inference and priors.
Kernel/linear, incremental/batch, dense/sparse and distributed/local variants retain computational and input contracts even where hypothesis spaces overlap.
Cross-package encoders, imputers, pipelines and neural networks retain missing-value, leakage, output and dependency distinctions; class names alone do not establish supersession.
General-purpose meta-estimators, FunctionTransformer and neural networks are not treated as superseding every model they could theoretically represent.
Survival, ordinal, spatial and forecasting specialists retain target, censoring, structure and output contracts.
